key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films are not just defects—they nucleate degradation at impurity–perovskite interfaces and can be rapidly detected before devices fail.
engineering_relevance: A fast, non-invasive microscopy-and-ML screening workflow can pre-qualify perovskite films for scalable manufacturing and early stability screening in tandem solar cells.
method: Nano-FTIR plus optical/scanning probe imaging to chemically identify impurities
Photo-stress testing to localize where degradation begins
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy with ML image analysis for seconds-level impurity detection
evidence_signal: The abstract reports chemically validated impurity identification and shows that films with higher impurity density exhibit faster early degradation, supporting impurity density as an early-warning stability metric.
watch_item: Performance depends on robust image/chemistry calibration, so the impurity classifier may need revalidation across perovskite compositions, processing routes, and imaging setups.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
